title: Asymptotically Log-Optimal Bayes-Assisted Confidence Sequences for Bounded Means
claim: Bayes-assisted methods give confidence sequences close to the oracle width while keeping cumulative miscoverage below the nominal level.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared log-n axis, shared bottom legend
description: Two line plots sit side by side with a shared legend underneath. Both use a log-scaled x-axis for sample size n, from 1 to 1000, and show five colored methods: empirical (orange), UP (green), MDP (red), BETEL (purple) and RETEL (brown). The left panel plots the confidence-sequence width ratio against the oracle. It has a dashed baseline at 1.0 and shaded bootstrap bands. The purple and brown curves spike early, then fall toward 1.0. The orange and green curves rise steadily toward 1.3–1.4 at large n. The right panel plots cumulative miscoverage as step-like curves with Wilson bands. A dashed line at α=0.1 sits above every curve, which all stay below it. The eye goes first to the tall purple peak and the diverging curves on the left.
caption: Synthetic beta-mixture experiment. The left and right panels show average CS length relative to the oracle and empirical cumulative miscoverage, respectively, over $1000$ replicates; the dashed line marks $\alpha = 0.1$. Width ratios use replicates where both the method and oracle CSs are non-empty. At $n=1000$, at most 2% are empty (0.8% on average). Shading shows pointwise 95% paired-bootstrap intervals for width ratios and Wilson intervals for cumulative miscoverage.
abstract: Confidence sequences based on test martingales provide time-uniform uncertainty quantification for the mean of bounded i.i.d. observations without parametric distributional assumptions. Their practical efficiency, however, depends strongly on the choice of martingale updates, and many existing constructions do not exploit prior information about plausible data-generating distributions or mean values. We propose a Bayes-assisted framework that uses a Bayesian working predictive model to adaptively construct confidence sequences. For each candidate mean and time point, the predictive distribution selects, among valid one-step martingale factors, the update maximising predictive expected log-growth; validity is therefore preserved even when the prior or working model is misspecified. We prove that if the predictive distribution is Wasserstein-consistent, the resulting procedure is asymptotically log-optimal, matching the per-sample log-growth of an oracle procedure with access to the true distribution. We instantiate the framework using robust predictives based on Dirichlet-process mixtures and Bayesian exponentially tilted empirical likelihood. Experiments on synthetic data, sequential best-arm identification for LLM evaluation, and prediction-powered inference show that informative priors can substantially reduce confidence-sequence width and sampling effort while retaining anytime-valid coverage.
